newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia looks at upgrading booming tourism.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia looks at upgrading booming tourism.

text.p: Tunisia earned a record 1.43 billion dinars ($1.34 billion) from tourism in 1996 and is forecasting a higher increase this year, Tourism and Handicrafts Minister Slaheddine Maaoui said on Monday.
Maaoui said Tunisia was also planning to expand, diversify and upgrade its tourism industry to attract more visitors.
"Foreign currency receipts in the tourism sector were 1.43 billion dinars in 1996, up by seven percent compared to 1995," he told Reuters in an interview. Receipts were 1.32 billion dinars in 1995.
Tourism is Tunisia's biggest foreign currency earner, making about 20 percent of its current receipts.

In 1996, the number of visitors from European countries rose seven percent to 2.53 million from 2.36 million. Europe is Tunisia's main market representing about 65 percent of the total arrivals in 1996.
German tourists kept the lead with 808,478 visitors in 1996, followed by 541,878 French tourists. British tourists arrivals fell 14 percent to 206,068 in 1996.
"Our objective is to have receipts reach $2.3 billion by the year 2000...," Maaoui said. Official forecasts put tourism revenues at $1.57 billion in 1997.
Most resorts were fully booked a week before the tourist season kicks off in April.

But Maaoui said he was disappointed tourists did not spend much money. He said Tunisia planned to promote sports activities and tours of ancient monuments in order to attract more upmarket tourists, in addition to those who come for the country's sunny and sandy beaches.
"The average daily expenditure of a tourist is now at $57. Our objective is to make him spend between $65 and $70 per day by the year 2001," he added.
"We want to build up on our mass-market tourism experience. We are seeking much higher quality to increase our economic performances. We want to put the cherry on the pudding," Maaoui said.

Six casinos, five of which have already opened or are to open in the next few months, were bound to make tourists spend more, he added. New five-star hotels will also be constructed in the next five years.
"We are looking at investors to establish a complex that could host international conferences in Tunis. We are already discussing a project with an Arab Gulf prince," he said without giving details.
Maaoui said that he expects investment in the tourism sector during the 1997-2001 period to amount to $1.48 billion, including 39,000 additional beds.
